styleBible: Photorealistic live-action Taiwanese workplace micro-film, grounded contemporary drama with real adult actors, natural skin texture, realistic hair and fabric, restrained facial acting, deliberate cinema-camera movement, motivated practical lighting, realistic glass reflections and full-bleed 16:9 framing. Every clip must look like footage from one coherent short film, never a visual novel or game screen. No anime, illustration, cel shading, character sprites, static cutouts, dialogue boxes, choice buttons, HUD, subtitles, captions, overlay text, split screen, logos or watermarks. Use only diegetic environmental sound; no voice-over and no music.
continuityBible: The story takes place in Taipei in 2026. The main event runs from 16:40 to 17:20 on one rainy workday. The company has already eliminated Lin Yu-cheng's position after losing its largest client; this is not a performance action and cannot be reversed in the meeting. Zhou Yu-an is still Lin's manager during the notification and must not seek forgiveness, romance, physical intimacy or emotional reassurance. HR partner Zeng Ya-lin witnesses the entire meeting and protects process boundaries. Only the true ending occurs three weeks later, after every employment, equipment, portfolio and recommendation process has ended, and Lin initiates private contact.

characterBible.zhou-yuan: Zhou Yu-an, age 31, Taiwanese department manager with an understated androgynous presentation, neat dark hair, pale dress shirt with a permanent crease at one cuff, dark trousers, office badge turned face-down before entering the meeting. Tension appears as attention to irrelevant details rather than dramatic emotion. The same live-action actor, face, hair and wardrobe must remain consistent across all clips.
characterBible.lin-yucheng: Lin Yu-cheng, age 26, Taiwanese product designer, short dark hair with very subtle pale gray-blue tips, a small MAKE IT OBVIOUS phrase printed on her T-shirt, an old digital watch and a pen clipped to her badge lanyard. Precise, observant and dryly composed; shock first appears through pauses, her watch, pen, gaze and controlled questions rather than crying. The same live-action actor, face, hair and wardrobe must remain consistent across all clips.
characterBible.zeng-yalin: Zeng Ya-lin, age 34, Taiwanese HR business partner, dark blazer with clean sneakers, carrying a tablet in a protective case. Calm, practical and nearly motionless; she sits closest to the door without blocking the exit and intervenes when process or boundaries are crossed. The same live-action actor, face, hair and wardrobe must remain consistent across all meeting clips.

propBible.rights-packet: One blue rights folder bearing Lin Yu-cheng's name. It represents the finalized position-elimination notice and rights information, never a coaching notebook, performance plan or action plan.
propBible.water-glasses: Three water glasses are on the Moon meeting-room table. Only Zeng Ya-lin's glass has been sipped before the conversation ends.
propBible.badges: Zhou Yu-an turns their badge face-down before the meeting; Lin Yu-cheng mirrors this action when leaving.
propBible.room: The Moon meeting room has glass walls, rain reflections and a small cartoon astronaut decal. Keep table, door, chair and window geography stable across all meeting clips.

items.requiredContinuity: Lin is still unaware that her position has been eliminated and continues working on the cancelled product. Zeng hands the finalized blue rights folder to Zhou. Rain has begun outside.
items.prompt: Opening scene of a live-action workplace micro-film in a cool blue Taipei open office at 16:40 while rain begins outside. Start close on Lin working at her monitor in the background, focused and unaware, then rack focus to Zeng approaching Zhou's desk with the blue rights folder held two centimetres above the surface before placing it down. Zhou reads Lin's name, glances toward her, and turns one cuff between tense fingers. Zeng remains composed beside the desk. Slow controlled lateral dolly, 50 mm lens, realistic monitor and window reflections, natural office movement. Do not reveal the folder as a performance review and do not show any game interface or dialogue box.

items.requiredContinuity: Zhou has the final folder. Lin has not yet been told the decision. Zeng is present nearby. The invitation establishes honesty or avoidance but does not turn the meeting into a discussion.
items.prompt: Second scene of the same live-action micro-film at 16:43. Over Zhou's shoulder, show a blank workplace chat composer without legible interface text as Zhou types, hesitates, deletes and finally sends a meeting invitation. In the middle distance, Lin's monitor receives a subtle notification glow; she reads, looks toward Zeng and notices the blue folder near Zhou. Her dry composure tightens for one beat as she saves her work. Zeng watches silently from two rows away. Use a restrained push-in, 50 mm lens and the same rain-blue office lighting. No floating message bubbles, no readable overlay, no celebratory tone and no implication that the meeting is optional.

items.requiredContinuity: All three people are present. Zhou's badge is already face-down. The blue folder and three glasses are visible. Lin learns that the completed decision eliminates her position and is not based on performance.
items.prompt: The irreversible notification scene in the same live-action micro-film. In the Moon glass meeting room at 17:00, frame all three adults in a stable medium-wide composition: Zhou opposite Lin, Zeng closest to the door without blocking it, the blue rights folder centred on the table and three water glasses visible, only Zeng's glass touched. Zhou's badge is face-down. Zhou states the decision with restrained directness; do not generate intelligible speech. Lin stops before fully settling into her chair, studies Zhou instead of the folder, then sits and lays the pen from her lanyard flat on the table. Zeng observes and is ready to correct procedure. Rain tracks down the glass behind them. Slow push-in on a 40 mm lens, real micro-expressions and breathing. This is a finalized position elimination, not coaching, performance feedback or a collaborative plan.

items.requiredContinuity: Zeng explains the document and alternative contact channel. Receiving is not agreement. Lin may take the folder for review and must never be pressured to sign immediately.
items.prompt: Procedure scene from the same live-action workplace micro-film at 17:12. Begin with a close insert of Zeng rotating the blue rights folder so it faces Lin but deliberately stopping it in the centre of the table rather than pushing it into her hands. Zeng opens to the rights pages and indicates separate sections with one calm finger. Lin checks her old digital watch, then places both hands away from the signature area and looks from the folder to Zeng. Zhou remains quiet in the edge of frame and does not touch the papers. Rack focus between folder, hands and faces; 65 mm lens, rain reflections and realistic paper movement. The scene must communicate time to review and an independent HR contact, never immediate consent, a performance plan or a demand for a signature.

items.requiredContinuity: Lin asks whether Zhou tried to keep her. Zhou may disclose the failed alternative proposal but must not turn that effort into emotional debt, confession or a request for gratitude. Zeng remains the witness.
items.prompt: Ethical climax of the same live-action micro-film at 17:18. Hold a close three-quarter profile on Lin as she asks a private question without generated intelligible dialogue; her gaze is steady and her thumb briefly lights the old digital watch. Cut focus within the same continuous composition to Zhou, who absorbs the question, glances once at the blue folder, then answers plainly with open empty hands and no attempt to move closer. Keep Zeng visible in soft focus near the door, attentive and prepared to intervene. The emotional tension comes from distance, eyelines and silence, not romance. Slow minimal dolly on a 50 mm lens. No touching, confession, pleading, gift, private payment, request for forgiveness or suggestion that Lin owes Zhou gratitude.

items.requiredContinuity: All employment, equipment, portfolio, recommendation and rights procedures are finished. Lin initiates the meeting. Neither person wears a company badge. This is the only branch that may suggest a future personal relationship.
items.prompt: True ending of the same live-action micro-film, exactly three weeks later in the warm Zero Platform cafe at night. The employment relationship and every company process are fully finished. Lin has chosen the public meeting place and sits where either person can leave freely. Neither person wears a company badge and no office props are present. Begin outside the cafe glass on two equal silhouettes, then drift inside to a balanced two-shot. Lin, still reserved and fully in control, slides one coffee toward Zhou and allows the smallest dry half-smile; Zhou receives it without reaching toward her or treating the moment as forgiveness. Warm practical lamps contrast with rain-dark glass. 50 mm lens, gentle human camera movement. No office, HR, blue folder, managerial posture, romantic embrace, kiss or triumphant happy-ending montage.

items.requiredContinuity: Lin takes the blue folder, knows the formal contact channel and leaves without promising private contact. Respect is shown by Zhou not asking for anything more.
items.prompt: Dignified ending of the same live-action workplace micro-film. In the Moon meeting room just after 17:20, Lin closes the blue rights folder, places it securely in her canvas bag and stands. She gives Zeng one clear professional nod, then looks briefly at Zhou without offering reassurance. At the door she turns her badge face-down and leaves on her own. Zhou remains seated and lets the silence stand; Zeng calmly records the completed handoff on her tablet. Hold the closed door and the two untouched water glasses for the final beat. Static 50 mm composition with subtle breathing and rain reflections. No smile promising reunion, private message, future work plan, romance or pursuit.

items.requiredContinuity: Lin left the blue folder behind in the Moon meeting room and required all further contact to go through Zeng; the folder remains there. At 22:14 Zhou considers a private apology in the open office but respects that boundary and sends nothing.
items.prompt: Soft Knife ending of the same live-action workplace micro-film at 22:14 in the nearly empty open office. Lin is no longer present, and the blue rights folder remains off-screen in the Moon meeting room. Start over Zhou's shoulder as a long unsent private message fills a phone or chat composer without legible text. A cleaner's vacuum passes far in the background. Zeng walks behind Zhou, pauses and gives one quiet boundary-setting look. Zhou selects the entire draft, deletes it, closes the composer and puts the phone face-down. Cool late-night monitor light, slow pullback on a 50 mm lens, diegetic air conditioning and distant vacuum only. No blue folder in this office shot, flashback, pursuit, sent message, reassurance, future promise or romance.

items.requiredContinuity: Zhou has crossed a professional boundary through an unauthorized private payment, confession or emotional pressure. Zeng immediately ends the conversation and takes control of formal follow-up. Lin refuses private contact and leaves.
items.prompt: Boundary-crossed ending of the same live-action workplace micro-film, beginning immediately after an unspecified professional boundary violation so it remains valid for either an unauthorized private-payment offer or a confession. In the Moon meeting room, Zeng decisively raises one hand, closes the blue folder and moves it to the HR side of the table. Lin's expression hardens into clarity rather than heartbreak. She removes the pen from the table, turns her badge face-down and leaves through the unobstructed door without accepting anything from Zhou. Zhou remains isolated across the table while Zeng documents the incident on her tablet. Controlled static 50 mm frame, cool hard reflections and uncomfortable room tone. No physical contact, money exchange, kiss, crying embrace, mutual confession, reconciliation or romantic framing.

postGenerationReview: Every frame is full-bleed live-action footage with no game UI, dialogue box, subtitles or overlay.
Actor identity, hair and wardrobe remain stable across clips.
Zeng Ya-lin is present in every Day 1 meeting-room clip and absent from the three-weeks-later cafe ending.
The blue folder, three glasses, badges, door, chairs and rain preserve branch-appropriate continuity.
No clip turns the layoff into coaching, a performance plan, future task planning or an optional discussion.
No romantic framing appears before the true ending's three-week time jump and Lin-initiated meeting.
